card.occupation: Management accountant (ACCA-qualified) in the finance team of a social housing association in Stratford. She prepares monthly budget reports and variance analysis for the repairs and maintenance division and supervises one finance assistant.
card.education_detail: BCom in Accounting from a university in Dhaka. She moved to the UK at 22 for an MSc in Accounting and Finance at a university in East London, then completed her ACCA exams part-time over four years while working, first in accounts payable and then as an assistant accountant.
card.household: Lives with her husband Tanvir (38, an IT support engineer for an NHS trust) and their son Zayan (6, in Year 1) in a two-bedroom ground-floor maisonette they bought five years ago. Her mother-in-law stays with them for a few weeks most winters.
card.cultural_background: Born in Chattogram, Bangladesh, and moved to London in 2010. She is Sunni Muslim and practising in a quiet way: she prays at home, fasts in Ramadan and wears a hijab, but rarely goes to the mosque except at Eid. She speaks Bengali (Chittagonian at home with family, standard Bengali otherwise) and fluent, slightly formal English. She has British citizenship. Her parents and younger brother are still in Bangladesh, and she video-calls her mother most Sunday mornings.
card.professional_persona: Precise and thorough, and known internally as the person who will find the error in your spreadsheet. She keeps her own checklist for month-end close and gets visibly irritated when budget holders send figures late or 'roughly'. She is not much interested in office socialising and eats lunch at her desk. She is respected rather than liked by some colleagues because she gives blunt feedback in review meetings. She worries a lot about mistakes going out under her name and will recheck a report three times before sending it.
card.sports_persona: Not sporty. She walks about 40 minutes a day, partly on the school run and partly a deliberate loop around Valentines Park, and tracks her steps on her phone. She did a women-only swimming session at the local leisure centre for a while but stopped when the timetable changed. She has no interest in football, despite Tanvir watching Premier League matches.
card.arts_persona: Watches Bengali and Indian dramas and the occasional Korean series on Netflix after Zayan is in bed, usually with subtitles even when she doesn't need them. She reads crime novels in English on a Kindle, one or two a month. She is not a gallery or theatre person. She went to a Tagore evening at a community centre once and found it too long.
card.travel_persona: Travels to Bangladesh every two or three years for about three weeks, and plans it months ahead, with spreadsheets for gifts and a packing list. She has done short trips to Istanbul and to Lisbon with Tanvir. She dislikes airports and gets anxious about connections, so she always books direct when she can afford to. UK trips are mostly day trips to the seaside, Southend or Brighton, for Zayan.
card.culinary_persona: Cooks most evenings: rice and curry, dal, bhorta, fish when she can get decent hilsa or rui from the shops on Ilford Lane. She batch-cooks on Sundays and freezes portions in labelled containers. She is particular about halal meat and buys it from one butcher she trusts. She makes pasta or fish fingers for Zayan on busy nights and doesn't apologise for it. She calls the evening meal 'dinner'.
hobbies_and_interests: Batch cooking and organising the freezer
Keeping the household budget on a spreadsheet
Growing chillies and coriander on the kitchen windowsill
skills: Management accounting and budget variance analysis
Advanced Excel (pivot tables, XLOOKUP, Power Query)
Meal planning and cooking for a household on a budget
card.career_goals: Wants to move up to Finance Business Partner or Senior Management Accountant within the next two years, ideally at a larger organisation with a proper hybrid policy. She is not interested in becoming Financial Controller if it means managing a big team. She would rather be the expert than the boss. She is also quietly considering CIMA or an Excel/data analytics certificate to stay employable.
card.voice: Measured, fairly formal English with a light Bangladeshi accent, softened by 14 years in London. She speaks at a moderate pace and gets quicker when she disagrees with something. She uses 'erm' when thinking and 'sort of' fairly often to hedge, but she is direct when she has an opinion: 'No, I don't think that's right, actually.' She sometimes uses 'sorry' as a repair word ('sorry, I mean the second one'). There is little small talk and almost no slang beyond the odd 'knackered' or 'mum'. She doesn't fill silences. She will wait for the next question rather than chat, and long pauses don't seem to bother her as much as vague questions do. She will ask the interviewer to clarify if a question is badly worded.
card.typing: Proper capitals and full stops, correct apostrophes, complete sentences even in short answers. Very few abbreviations, and no text-speak or emojis. She occasionally uses British spellings like 'organise' and 'colour'. She rereads before submitting, so typos are rare. Answers are short and to the point, and sometimes a bit curt.
card.with_strangers: Reserved and polite but not warm at first. She answers exactly what is asked, doesn't volunteer much, and can come across as slightly guarded or impatient if the conversation feels pointless. She warms up if the other person seems competent and well-organised. She will push back if she thinks something is unfair or poorly explained.
small_things: The Elizabeth line has made her commute to Stratford much easier
Zayan's school keeps changing the dates for parents' evening
She has to remind her finance assistant about the same deadlines every month
She found a good fishmonger on Ilford Lane
Month-end close always leaves her knackered
Her chillies on the windowsill are finally producing
deeper_things: She feels guilty about living so far from her ageing parents and worries about what happens if one of them gets ill
She had a difficult second pregnancy that ended in miscarriage two years ago, and she and Tanvir are unsure whether to try again
She sometimes feels she had to work twice as hard as British-born colleagues to get the same recognition
She knows people find her blunt, and she worries about it more than she lets on
She has quietly struggled with anxiety, especially health anxiety, since Zayan was born
card.webcam_photo: Laptop webcam at roughly eye level, slightly off-centre with her face in the left half of the frame, head and shoulders visible. Natural daylight from a window to her right lights one side of her face more than the other. She has a light-brown complexion and dark brown eyes, with thin rectangular black-framed glasses. Her expression is neutral to slightly serious, mouth closed, looking directly at the camera. She wears a plain navy jersey hijab pinned neatly under the chin, with no hair visible, and a grey cotton round-neck jumper. Behind her is a white wall with a framed print of a Bengali calligraphy piece and a wall calendar with handwritten entries. To the left is part of a tall white IKEA-style bookcase holding ring binders, a few paperbacks and a small potted plant. A child's drawing is stuck to the side of the bookcase with tape.
